reason: The contract the thin model replaces: what running install.py against another repository establishes today. Basis of decision D2, grounded in the 2026-08-09 fleet sweep of all 8 consumers: no consumer CI executes pack code. Seven are lint-only (bash -n / node --check) or shellcheck globs; the single functional call, anomaly-metric-creator ci.yml:293 running pr-body-scope.py, passes neither --body-file nor the PR-body env vars, so it prints categories and exits 0 unconditionally and has never blocked a PR. Decision (user, 2026-08-09): drop that step during migration. The 'consumer CI executes pack code' category is therefore empty fleet-wide and no pinned-fetch bootstrap is needed. anomaly-metric-creator also carries sd-ai-command-pack-sync.yml, the vendoring sync automation, which the thin model deletes rather than migrates.

Manifest-driven install and version semantics, which the plugin model has to reproduce or replace. Basis of decision D1, grounded in the 2026-08-09 Claude Code plugin capability review: update signal resolves plugin.json version -> marketplace version -> commit SHA -> archive sha256, so release-prep can stamp plugin.json from manifest.json and make plugin updates track pack releases exactly. One installed version per machine per scope, with no per-project selection -- which satisfies requirement 2's one-action-machine-wide propagation and makes the consumer-repo pin an expectation record for fleet reporting, not a control over what executes. Cross-machine skew stays possible and must be surfaced by sd-status. Three gaps carried into design: non-Claude surfaces (.agents/, Codex, Gemini) that a plugin does not carry, .claude/rules/ project-context semantics with no CLAUDE.md injection, and skills that hardcode repo-relative scripts/ paths needing ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} or bin-name invocation.
